change.title: pr-36880-flat
change.description: Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: V2 canView() ignores the MANAGE scope, so manage-all-clients does not imply list/view
findings.body:
`canView()` is `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW)` (lines 86-88). It never checks the MANAGE scope. In V1, `canView()` includes manage (`ClientPermissions.java:287-289`). `UserPermissionsV2.canView` accepts VIEW or MANAGE (`UserPermissionsV2.java:52`).

`ClientsResource.getClients` calls `auth.clients().requireList()` first (`ClientsResource.java:120`), and `canList()` is `canView() || QUERY_CLIENTS/QUERY_USERS role` (`ClientPermissions.java:240-244`). An admin whose only grant is an all-clients MANAGE permission therefore gets 403 when listing clients. The same applies to `canListClientScopes()` and `canViewClientScopes()`, which both reduce to `canView()`. That admin can still create or manage client scopes (`canManageClientScopes`, line 106).

`canView(ClientScopeModel)` (line 118-122) does accept MANAGE, so the client-scope methods contradict each other.

`testManageAllClients` does not catch this. `myadmin` has the `query-users` role (`RealmAdminPermissionsConfig.java:34`), which satisfies `canList()` on its own.

Fix: in `canView()` also return true for `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Add a test where the admin has no query role.

findings.title: Client removal throws UnsupportedOperationException when V1 and V2 FGAP are both enabled
findings.body:
The listener body is now gated on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1). `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever V2 is enabled (line 67). Its `clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` always throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195).

If both features are on, deleting any client fires `ClientRemovedEvent` and reaches line 91. The exception escapes the listener and client deletion fails. Both features can be on together: `TOKEN_EXCHANGE_STANDARD_V2` depends on V1 (`Profile.java:77`), and nothing makes V1 and V2 exclusive. The same combination also makes `PUT clients/{id}/management/permissions` (V1-gated, `ClientResource.java:739-742`) fail with a 500.

Before this PR, `clients()` in V2 mode was the inherited V1 class, so this combination did not throw.

Fix options: skip the `ClientRemovedEvent` branch when V2 is enabled, or make `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` a no-op. Add a test that deletes a client with the V2 feature on.

findings.title: Existing V2 realms lack the Clients resource and new scopes; possible NPE/ModelException
findings.body:
`AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the realm already has an admin-permissions client (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226-228`). A realm that enabled V2 permissions before this PR was therefore created with only the `Users` type resource and no `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope` or `map-roles-composite` scopes.

For such a realm, `getResourceTypeResource(..., "Clients")` returns null at line 217, and line 219 then calls `findByResource(server, null)`. Creating a per-client permission would hit `ModelException("No scopes found.")` (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:108`).

`getResourceTypeResource` also returns null when the realm's admin-permissions flag is switched off after the client exists. `UserPermissionsV2` has the same shape. Is there a migration for realms initialised before this change, or is the experimental feature allowed to break them? If not, guard the null resource at line 217 (return false).

findings.title: canExchangeTo throws in V2, turning a token-exchange denial into a 500
findings.body:
`AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` calls `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(client, targetClient, token)` whenever the audience client differs from the caller (`AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276`). With V2 enabled, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, so this now reaches line 149 and throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. The caller gets a 500 instead of the 403 "Client not allowed to exchange" at lines 277-280.

Before this PR the inherited V1 implementation answered `false`, or evaluated V1 permissions. Is a V2 plus legacy token-exchange setup meant to be unsupported? If so, say it explicitly. Otherwise return `false` here, as the old behaviour did when no V1 permission existed.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports
findings.body:
`getEvaluationContext` (lines 262-272) is never called. It is a copy of the V1 token-exchange evaluation context, left over after `canExchangeTo` was made to throw. Its removal also leaves unused: `Scope`, `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `logger`, `EvaluationContext`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, and `AccessToken` apart from the `canExchangeTo` signature.

`hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` and `hasPermission(String)` (lines 207-260) duplicate the evaluate-and-scan loop and could share one helper. `hasGrantedPermission` (274-286) is a third copy.

Separately, `getClientsWithPermission` filters `findByType(server, "Clients")` (line 138). The type resource itself is created with that type (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:249-250`), so it may be added to `granted` under the name `Clients`. The method has no caller in `services` today.

findings.title: Javadoc on void require* methods says they return true
findings.body: `requireView()` (line 89) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 101) are `void`, but their javadoc says "Returns {@code true} if ...". They should read "Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns {@code false}", like the neighbouring require* methods.

findings.title: JUnit 4 fail import; tests leak state; gaps in coverage
findings.body:
1. Line 25 imports `org.junit.Assert.fail` (JUnit 4). Every other class in this package uses `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.fail`. Switch to the jupiter import.

2. The tests mutate the shared `myclient`/realm and never revert it, so they depend on test order within the class:
- `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient`, moves a default scope to optional, and picks scopes by `get(1)`.
- `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates `myclient-role` and `myclient-subRole`, adds a role mapping to `myadmin`, and registers no cleanup.

3. Missing coverage:
- VIEW granted on a single client.
- `map-roles-client-scope`.
- Deleting a client while V2 is enabled, which is the path the `AdminPermissions` listener change affects.
- An admin with MANAGE or VIEW on all clients and no `query-users` role. `myadmin` has `query-users`, so `canList()` is satisfied regardless.

4. `testViewAllClients` calls `clients().create(null)`. This passes only because the 403 happens before the body is parsed. Use `newClient` instead.

findings.title: Whitespace-only line added
findings.body: The blank line after the class declaration was replaced by a line containing four spaces. It is an unintended whitespace change and should be reverted.

contracts.action: Client removal event listener now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled
contracts.equivalent_path: Same listener before the change ran unconditionally. management() picks V1 or V2 on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 (AdminPermissions.java:66-71).
contracts.before_after: Before: with V2 on, ClientRemovedEvent called the inherited V1 ClientPermissions.setPermissionsEnabled(false), which was harmless. After: it is skipped when V1 is off. When V1 and V2 are both on it reaches ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throws.
contracts.visible_effect: Deleting a client with both features enabled fails with a server error. With V2 only, nothing changes visibly.
contracts.failure_mode: UnsupportedOperationException propagates out of the provider event listener and aborts client removal.

contracts.action: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() decides who may list clients and client scopes
contracts.equivalent_path: V1 ClientPermissions.canView (manage or view default roles), and UserPermissionsV2.canView, which accepts VIEW or MANAGE scopes.
contracts.before_after: V1 and Users V2 treat manage as implying view. Clients V2 canView() checks only the VIEW scope and the default admin roles.
contracts.visible_effect: An admin with all-clients MANAGE and no query role gets 403 on GET clients and on client-scope listing.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent permission gap rather than a crash. The current test hides it because myadmin holds query-users.

contracts.action: hasPermission(client, scope) loads the per-client resource, or falls back to the 'Clients' type resource, and evaluates it
contracts.equivalent_path: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission (same shape). It also filters returned permissions by resource id, which the client version does not.
contracts.before_after: Users: findByName(server, user.getId()), then the type resource, then evaluatePermission. Clients: the same, using the 3-argument findByName with owner server.getId().
contracts.visible_effect: Per-client and all-clients FGAP grants decide client admin access.
contracts.failure_mode: If the Clients type resource is missing (realm initialised before this PR, or the flag switched off), findByResource(server, null) is called with a null resource.
contracts.open_question: Is there a migration that adds the Clients resource and the new scopes to realms whose admin-permissions client already exists?

contracts.action: Token exchange to another client calls clients().canExchangeTo under V2
contracts.equivalent_path: V1 ClientPermissions.canExchangeTo (ClientPermissions.java:328-371) returns false when nothing is configured.
contracts.before_after: Before: V1 logic evaluated, or returned false, giving a 403 'Client not allowed to exchange'. After: with V2 enabled it throws UnsupportedOperationException.
contracts.visible_effect: Token exchange to a different audience client returns a 500 instead of an access_denied response.
contracts.failure_mode: Unhandled runtime exception in the token endpoint.

contracts.action: AdminPermissionsSchema registers the Clients resource type and resolves client ids or clientIds to resource names
contracts.before_after: Same pattern as users: look up by internal id, then by clientId, and return client.getId() as the resource name. Scopes and the type resource are created only in init, which is skipped when the admin-permissions client already exists.
contracts.visible_effect: Permissions can be created for a client by id or clientId.
contracts.failure_mode: For pre-existing realms the new scopes and type resource are absent, so creation throws ModelException 'No scopes found.'.
contracts.open_question: Is there a migration for realms where the admin-permissions client was created before the Clients type existed?

contracts.action: Test class now calls the static helpers getScopePermissionsResource(client) and createPermission(client, permission) instead of the former instance versions
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous no-arg helpers in AbstractPermissionTest, which used the injected admin-permissions client field
contracts.before_after: Before, the helpers used the injected `client` field implicitly. Now the same `client` field (@InjectClient attached to ADMIN_PERMISSIONS_CLIENT_ID) is passed explicitly, and the helpers call client.admin().authorization().permissions().scope() (AbstractPermissionTest.java:54-74). Behaviour is unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: createPermission still asserts the expected HTTP status (201 by default) and closes the Response. @AfterEach cleanup is unchanged.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** The V2 client permission evaluator largely mirrors the V2 users one, but I found two defects (manage-all-clients doesn't imply list/view; V1+V2 client deletion throws) and several smaller issues.

- **Manage doesn't imply list/view (fix):** `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` ignores the MANAGE scope. An admin with all-clients MANAGE and no query role would get 403 on listing clients and client scopes. The tests miss this because `myadmin` has `query-users`.
- **Client deletion with V1 and V2 both on (fix):** the `AdminPermissions` listener is now gated on the V1 feature, and `management()` returns the V2 evaluator when V2 is on. With both features enabled, removing a client hits `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws.
- **Consider:**
  - Token exchange to another client throws in V2 (500 instead of 403).
  - Realms whose admin-permissions client already exists never get the `Clients` resource or the new scopes, which can cause a null-resource failure.
  - Dead code and unused imports in `ClientPermissionsV2`.
  - Wrong javadoc on the `void require*` methods.
  - Test hygiene and coverage: the JUnit 4 `fail` import, leaked state between tests, and no test for client deletion under V2.
  - A stray whitespace-only line in `AdminPermissionsSchema`.

I read the diffs of `PermissionRESTTest.java` and `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java` and found nothing to flag; both are mechanical changes to the new helper signatures. I did not read either file in full.

**Batch 2 of 2.** UserResourceTypePermissionTest only changes its calls to pass the injected `client` into the now-static helpers in AbstractPermissionTest. I checked every call site and the helper signatures, and the behaviour is unchanged. I found nothing to flag.
